title: Submit a ticket — round 5: highlights without hard lines, every fold on the shared row, Contribute's failures, tag colours

steps.path: Settings → Performance → an opened row, pointer on its header
steps.headline: Pointing at an opened row lights the whole box — no strip across the top ending in a hard line.
steps.changed: Round 4 lit only the header, with a hard edge where the opened text began. Now the box itself lights, open or closed.
steps.notice: Every folded row in the app behaves this way; the pictures below show each one.

steps.path: Assistant settings → Permissions → a folder, opened and pointed at
steps.headline: Found in the same sweep: a Permissions folder now lights as one box, not as a band ending above its rules.
steps.changed: Its header used to tint edge to edge and stop in a hard line above the opened rules.
steps.notice: Same shape and contents; only the highlight changed.

steps.path: Session → What the assistant was given → Skills → a skill
steps.headline: A skill's fold is now the shared folded row: it lights as one box, with no line between its name and its text.
steps.changed: It was a hand-built card with a divider line under the header and a header-only highlight.

steps.headline: Additional customizations is now the shared folded row; its settings open inside it.
steps.changed: It was a hand-built fold. It looks almost the same; its outline now matches every other folded row.

steps.headline: Fine-tune glass opens its sliders inside its own box instead of below it.
steps.changed: The sliders used to sit loose under the row.

steps.path: Settings → Assistant → Local models → a model's Settings
steps.headline: A model's Advanced settings open inside the Advanced box.
steps.changed: They used to sit under the row as separate boxes.

steps.path: Settings → Assistant → Local models → Local engine → Advanced
steps.headline: The engine's Advanced settings open inside the Advanced box, without the indent.
steps.changed: They used to hang under the row, indented.

steps.headline: A failed download is now the red notice box with Try again inside, under what Contribute is for.
steps.changed: Was a grey box with a bold title and a Retry button — the older error look.
steps.notice: Same reason shown; nothing is left behind, so trying again starts cleanly.

steps.headline: If the conversation won't open, the same red notice box says so, with Try again.
steps.changed: Was the older grey error box with a title.
steps.notice: It still says where the code is.

steps.path: Tags such as Submitted, Installed, Online, Sync problem — on every screen
steps.headline: Should every coloured tag be easier to see? It changes tags across the whole app.
steps.today: A tag's colour is a faint tint behind grey words. On all 14 themes, green (Submitted, Online, Synced) is the faintest; on YouCoded it reads grey.
steps.problem: Too faint to see at a glance, so the colour says nothing.
steps.proposal: Pick one. Nothing changes in the app yet.
steps.measured: Colour difference behind the tag, lowest on any theme: green 8.4 → 26.9; grey in a card 2.5 → 5.9 (under 5 is hard to see).

options.label: Stronger tags
pros: Green, amber and red read as colours on every theme
Grey tags stay visible inside cards
cons: Every tag in the app gets a little heavier

options.label: Keep today's
cons: Green tags read grey on light themes

steps.headline: May a card hold a short bulleted list of facts, like Contribute's three lines?
steps.today: Contribute's card says what it does in one sentence, then three bullet points: the first-time 1 GB download, that your app and files don't change, and what opens next.
steps.problem: The design guide doesn't say whether a list belongs in a card. Everywhere else, facts are rows or sentences.
steps.proposal: Pick one; the guide records it either way.

options.label: Allow short lists
pros: Three separate facts read faster as a list
Keeps Contribute as approved last round
cons: One more look the guide allows

options.label: Sentences only
pros: One less look in the app
cons: Contribute's three facts become a longer paragraph

options.label: Rows
cons: Rows suggest something to click; these are just facts

steps.surface: Two other places the sweep found
steps.path: Git review side panel; Open tasks popup
steps.headline: Fix two more hard edges the sweep found, the same way?
steps.today: Git review: each commit card's header lights edge to edge when pointed at and stops in a hard line above the opened changes. Open tasks: a full-width line sits above the "Inactive" heading.
steps.problem: The same hard line you didn't like on the folded rows. Neither has a practice screen, so there are no pictures of them yet.
steps.proposal: Yes: the commit card lights as one box, and the Open tasks line goes (spacing instead). No: leave them.
